identity.fantasy: A massive-weapon berserker who builds Fury through crushing swings and Whirls, then turns wounded enemies into execute fuel.
identity.one_line: A massive-weapon berserker who builds Fury through crushing swings and Whirls, then turns wounded enemies into execute fuel. The defining decision is contextual: The player reacts mainly to sub-35-percent timing and reset opportunities.

mechanics.core_loop: A heavy-weapon brawler built around large swings, Whirls, Storm of Steel, and execute attacks such as Decapitate. It wants to build momentum and Fury, then cash out below 35% health; it has strong cleave and self-sustain, but its best damage requires melee uptime and correct execute timing.
mechanics.single_target: Build Fury and heavy-hit momentum with Whirls and Storm of Steel, use Crush to establish Break where the party does not supply it, then reserve Decapitate and reset effects for the sub-35-percent execute phase. No captured source establishes a universal exact priority.
mechanics.aoe: Whirls and Storm of Steel provide cleave, but current players describe the early pack game as weaker than the single-target execute plan. Applying Break manually can consume several globals before the damage loop begins.
mechanics.movement_and_target_switching: Mostly conventional melee pursuit, with uptime more important than intricate movement tech.
mechanics.defense_and_control: Its structural defensive package includes Decapitate, Overkill, Battering Ram, Whirling Assault, Steelslinger.
mechanics.group_utility: Group or control tools include Crush, Horde Breaker, Symbol of the Warspear, Utter Devastation.

failure_modes.text: Losing melee contact, delaying the execute cash-out, or spending five globals establishing Break can erase the payoff of the spec's slow heavy-weapon setup.
Applying Break after the burst should have started delays every heavy payoff that follows.
A weak or outdated weapon magnifies the downtime between slow attacks and can make the late leveling band feel much worse.
